\section[\texorpdfstring{\ru{газета} (gazéta)}{газета (gazéta)}]{\ru{газета} (gazéta) — a newspaper}

\label{lesson:RU-C192-gazeta}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Russian for a charger; morning exercises, then the Russian for a laptop.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ru{газета}}
\textbf{\ru{газета}} (\emph{gazéta}) — \textquotedblleft{}a newspaper\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ru{газета}} comes from Italian \emph{gazzetta}, the source also of French \emph{gazette}; Vasmer traces it to Venetian \emph{gazeta}, a small coin paid for the news sheet.
\end{cousinweb}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ru{журнал}}
\textbf{\ru{журнал}} (\emph{zhurnál}) — \textquotedblleft{}a magazine\textquotedblright{}.

\textbf{\ru{журнал}} — from 1720, written \emph{\ru{юрнал}} by Peter the Great; it comes from French \emph{journal}, from Medieval Latin \emph{diurnālis}, \textquotedblleft{}daily\textquotedblright{} (Vasmer).
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ru{словарь} (slovár)}{словарь (slovár)}]{\ru{словарь} (slovár) — a dictionary}

\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Russian for a newspaper, then the Russian for a magazine.

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ru{словарь}}
\textbf{\ru{словарь}} (\emph{slovár}) — \textquotedblleft{}a dictionary\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ru{словарь}} is \emph{\ru{слово}}, \textquotedblleft{}a word\textquotedblright{}, with \emph{-\ru{арь}}, a suffix for a thing or keeper: a book of words. \emph{\ru{Слово}} $\leftarrow$ Proto-Slavic \emph{*slovo} — inherited; Vasmer relates it to Sanskrit \emph{śrávas}, \textquotedblleft{}fame\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ru{линейка} (linéyka)}{линейка (linéyka)}]{\ru{линейка} (linéyka) — a ruler}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ru{линейка}}
\textbf{\ru{линейка}} (\emph{linéyka}) — \textquotedblleft{}a ruler\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ru{линейка}} comes from \emph{\ru{линея}}, an older form of \emph{\ru{линия}}, \textquotedblleft{}a line\textquotedblright{} (Vasmer), with \emph{-\ru{йка}}; \emph{\ru{линия}} came through Polish \emph{linia} or German \emph{Linie} from Latin \emph{līnea}, \textquotedblleft{}a linen thread\textquotedblright{}, from \emph{līnum}, \textquotedblleft{}flax\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}
